candidates.title: Kill Jackie
candidates.reason: Completed eight-episode action/crime thriller with a sustained pursuer-versus-pursued structure rather than a procedural mystery. Jackie learns that the Seven Demons have been hired to kill her and responds by hunting the assassins one by one; episode-level evidence shows alliances, hostage situations and deals repeatedly changing the tactical picture through the back half, while the finale resolves the remaining Demons and forces Jackie to confront the reason she was targeted. Whole-runtime evidence identifies Sam, her trusted lawyer and romantic partner, as the person behind the hit, a late betrayal that materially reframes the threat. Reviews consistently describe the season as fast, action-packed and convoluted, with substantial gunfights/chases and dark comedy. The fit is therefore strongest in cat-and-mouse, psychological strategy, deception, suspense, action density and brutality, with moderate progressive revelation and revelation frequency rather than mystery/investigation. Weaknesses are equally material: the show is shallow/cartoonish according to reviews, interpersonal material is significant, the central mystery is not the primary engine for much of the runtime, and much of the forward motion comes from action confrontations rather than clue-puzzling.

research_rejections.title: Drishyam: The Conclusion
research_rejections.reason: Qualitatively very promising for the profile: the Sameer Deshmukh case is reopened, police search for loopholes in Vijay's cover story, and multiple fresh reviews describe strong suspense, cat-and-mouse play and a major climax. However, the canonical IMDb title identity could not be resolved confidently from the consulted sources in this run. The research runbook requires uncertain identities to stay out of candidates, so no 30-dimension measurement is invented for it here. It should be reconsidered once the canonical IMDb identity is independently confirmed.
